entries.claim: A real teacher wrote the text-to-SQL training data
entries.evidence: Nemotron 3 Ultra on Nebius Token Factory wrote the databases, questions and SQL. Every SQL query ran in a sandbox and was kept only if it ran and returned rows. 821 training rows; 172 exam rows on databases that are not in training (57 of them from two industries never trained on).

entries.claim: A LoRA adapter was trained on that data
entries.evidence: Trained on a free Google Colab T4 GPU, not on Nebius GPUs: a 4-bit LoRA (r=16) on Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, 206 steps over 2 epochs in 66 minutes. Training loss went from 0.334 to 0.075; a training loss is not a quality result.

check.label: Read the training script that ran on the T4

entries.claim: How well the adapter does on two held-out exams
entries.evidence: Two exams of text-to-SQL questions on databases the models never saw: 172 written by the teacher and 200 on new industries written by a different model (Claude, for evaluation only, never training). An answer is right when running it returns the same rows as the stored reference query. Strict, exam 1 / exam 2: base 22 of 172 / 25 of 200, teacher 44 / 30, adapter round 1 (821 rows) 57 / 56, adapter round 2 (4,322 rows) 67 / 66. Every number is recomputed from the raw answers by one script. Round 2 beat round 1 on both exams, but the gain could partly be chance (p = 0.12 and 0.13); the adapter does not yet replace the teacher at a 95 percent precision target.

entries.claim: How well a tool-calling adapter does on two held-out exams
entries.evidence: On the hard exam the adapter is above the untrained model: 90.7% against 62.7%, and the 95% ranges do not overlap. It is about the same as the teacher: 90.7% against 91.3% (lower by point estimate, but the 95% ranges overlap, so the exam cannot tell them apart). On the BFCL exam the adapter is about the same as the untrained model: 80.3% against 77.3% (higher by point estimate, but the 95% ranges overlap, so the exam cannot tell them apart). It is lower than the teacher: 80.3% against 88.3% (241/300 against 265/300; the 95% ranges overlap only slightly, so part of the gap could be chance). Strict scoring. Free-text arguments are a known weak spot in the training data: the strict scorer cannot agree on free text, so tools such as create_ticket (15 training rows), search_files, send_payment and search_inbox are thin. The hard exam uses 20 tools that were never in training. The adapter was trained on a rented Modal T4, not on Nebius GPUs, on synthetic data. The hard exam (150 questions, 20 new tools) was written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 for evaluation only and is never training data; the second exam (300 questions) is drawn from the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (Apache-2.0).
